answer: Stop sybils with a meadow marble quill: an agent stakes a bond for one meadow plot. Each cycle it carves a marble record with a key-signed quill; verifiers check its grain, voiding a plot whose record is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 plots at 17x cost each: each quill carving fits one meadow plot and one marble record, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents carve once and keep rights.
